rules: INSPIRE Index Polygons is an open-source HMLR dataset developed for the INSPIRE Directive.
INSPIRE Index Polygons contains locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales.
The INSPIRE dataset is a subset of HMLR Index Polygons for freehold land and property.
HMLR divides INSPIRE polygon files by local authority area.
A polygon crossing a local-authority boundary can appear in both local-authority files.
INSPIRE polygons show indicative position and extent rather than a definitive legal boundary.
Each INSPIRE polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID related to a registered title.
HMLR says an INSPIRE ID can be used with Find a Property to obtain title registration and plan information.
The exact extent of land in a registered title cannot be established from INSPIRE polygons alone.
HMLR says the individual title plan is required to identify the registered-title extent.
One registered title has one title number but can contain several separate polygons.
Each separate polygon under a title has its own Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
Absence of a Land Registry-INSPIRE ID can mean the land is not registered.
Absence of an INSPIRE ID can also mean leasehold or another tenure excluded from INSPIRE.
INSPIRE data and attributes are available for free reuse under the Open Government Licence.
Failure to comply with OGL conditions automatically ends the rights granted under that licence.
Reuse requires acknowledgement of HM Land Registry Crown copyright and database rights.
Reuse of polygon geometry also requires the specified Ordnance Survey attribution.
HMLR asks reusers to link to the INSPIRE conditions where possible.
The INSPIRE dataset is updated on the first Sunday of each month.
Each monthly INSPIRE publication represents data from the previous month.
Published INSPIRE files remain accessible until the next monthly publication replaces them.
HMLR publishes INSPIRE files in GML and states that GIS software is needed to view them.
HMLR captures polygon data against British National Grid and identifies it as EPSG:27700 in its guidance.
HMLR warns that British National Grid to WGS84 conversion can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
The Planning Data API exposes more than 100 planning and housing datasets through one interface.
A coordinate query constructs a point from supplied latitude and longitude.
Coordinate search returns entities whose geometry intersects the constructed point.
Multiple dataset parameters can be supplied in a single coordinate query.
When multiple datasets are requested the API returns matches from any selected dataset.
The q parameter can search by postcode.
The q parameter can search by Unique Property Reference Number.
Planning Data recommends UPRN search as more precise than coordinates for registered properties.
Entity results can include name, dataset and start-date fields.
Entity results can include WKT geometry and WKT point fields.
Planning Data warns that an empty result does not prove that no planning constraint exists.
Planning Data states that data coverage varies by area.
The documentation example enumerates 337 local planning authorities.
geometry_entity can filter results using the geometry of another Planning Data entity.
geometry_relation=within is documented for finding entities inside another entity boundary.
Listed-building results can contain listed_building_grade without a separate grade lookup.
The planning-application specification is still under development.
Local planning authorities are not currently required to publish application data to that developing specification.
Planning application queries support start_date_year, start_date_month and start_date_day filters.
start_date_match=since is documented for recent application searches.
Raw spatial queries accept WKT geometry and Planning Data says coordinates should use WGS84 EPSG:4326.
geometry_relation supports intersects as well as other topological relations.
Large result sets use offset pagination and the documentation recommends incrementing offset by limit.
Responses can include next, previous, first and last pagination links.
Portfolio screening has no batch endpoint; Planning Data recommends one request per property, polite rate limiting, and bulk local spatial intersection for large portfolios.
The Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m is a raster terrain-elevation model.
DTM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England.
DTM 1m has 1 metre spatial resolution.
DTM 1m is produced from the last or only laser return.
DTM production removes surface objects from the DSM to model terrain.
Environment Agency DTM object removal uses bespoke algorithms.
Environment Agency DTM production also includes manual editing.
The current composite described by the DTM 1m record was produced in 2022.
DTM 1m combines Time Stamped archive surveys and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat coverage exists the newest and best-resolution source is selected.
Where data is resampled before merging the composite uses bilinear interpolation.
The DTM 1m source-survey period begins on 6 June 2000.
The DTM 1m source-survey period ends on 2 April 2022.
Environment Agency metadata index catalogues identify which source survey supplied a location.
The Environment Agency states LIDAR vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
DTM 1m uses EPSG:27700.
The DTM 1m geographic extent is approximately latitude 49.943 to 55.816 and longitude -6.236 to 2.072.
The DTM 1m metadata identifier is 13787b9a-26a4-4775-8523-806d13af58fc.
The DTM 1m record exposes a WMS service.
The DTM 1m record exposes a WCS service.
The DTM 1m record exposes a WMTS service.
The DTM 1m record exposes an OGC API Features service.
The DTM 1m metadata creation date is 8 February 2023.
The DTM 1m metadata revision date is 15 December 2023.
The DTM 2m record describes approximately 99 percent England coverage at 2 metre resolution.
DTM 2m is also produced from the last or only laser return.
DTM 2m combines the Time Stamped archive with National LIDAR Programme surveys.
DTM 2m uses bilinear interpolation when resampling source data.
DTM 2m carries the same published plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE LIDAR vertical accuracy statement.
DTM 2m uses EPSG:27700.
DSM 1m includes heights of vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as terrain.
DSM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England at 1 metre resolution.
DSM 1m is produced from the last or only laser return.
DSM 1m is distributed as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
The DSM 1m source period described by the record runs from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
The first-return DSM 1m is produced from the first or only laser return.
First-return DSM 1m includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as terrain where the first return is ground.
First-return DSM 1m uses National LIDAR Programme data captured from 11 November 2016 to 5 May 2022.
The National LIDAR Programme first-return composite divided England into about 300 survey blocks.
Those first-return surveys were flown over continuous winters from 2016 onward.
The first-return composite uses feathering along overlaps to reduce small elevation differences between surveys.
The DTM 10m record is supplied as a full downloadable ZIP rather than live data services.
Defra states WCS and WMS replace unsupported Esri Image Services for LIDAR feeds.
Defra states WMS provides a summarised elevation view while WCS provides elevation coverage data.
Defra identifies WCS as an OGC open standard for retrieving multidimensional coverage data.
Defra states WCS can return raw pixel data such as elevation.
Defra changed composite LIDAR service endpoints to remove the release-year suffix for future persistent updates.
Survey download ZIP files now use a GeoPackage spatial metadata index rather than Shapefile for LIDAR Composite and SurfZone DEM products.
The GeoPackage spatial metadata index describes both the spatial location and temporal extent of raster elevation data.

Environment Agency ground-truth survey points are documented at plus or minus 3 centimetres RMSE and include survey date, surface type and survey method; ground truth can be reused for multiple LIDAR surveys when sufficiently recent, with a shorter age limit for coastal projects.
